own_historical_cartilage001_source.evidence: Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade cartilage loss, weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. 8 x 5 mm full-thickness cartilage defect posterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. High grade partial thickness cartilage loss of the tibial plateau.
own_historical_cartilage001_source.rationale: The 8 by 5 mm full-thickness focus does not establish a centimeter-scale defect or bound the surrounding high-grade disease. Generic diffuse high-grade femoral loss has no explicit fraction, and tibial high-grade partial-thickness loss lacks extent; uncertain rather than using the small focus for an overall negative.

own_new_preproposal_source.evidence: Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade cartilage loss, weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. 8 x 5 mm full-thickness cartilage defect posterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. own_new_preproposal_source.rationale: Diffuse high-grade cartilage loss across the weightbearing femoral region supplies qualifying depth and qualitative broad extent. The separately measured8x5mm full-thickness defect does not restrict the extent of the preceding diffuse high-grade loss. This is a disclosed report-level regional-extent inference, not a new numeric measurement or an image reread.

new_root_proposal.reason: I retain my original source-frozen uncertainty. Low-grade cartilage fraying is not a directly stated less-than-half loss fraction or explicit preserved-thickness/superficial-only description. Both cartilage001 readers interpreted it as below threshold; those opinions remain preserved. The analogous earlier mild-fraying corrections were separately retired after source reassessment. This new proposal needs a distinct actual assessment, and is not accepted merely because it is more conservative.
